patch.value: Built-in help examples teach an explicit --author on dozens of commands, training every agent to suppress its own detected identity and pay tokens for it

src/cli/help-content.ts publishes --author "codex-agent" or --assignee codex-agent in the canonical examples for claim, release, close, delete, restore, comments, history-compact, activity, create, list, next, calendar, ctx and more, and src/cli/register-operations.ts repeats it for claim and start-task. An agent reading help learns that passing an author is normal pm usage. Two costs follow. First, correctness: an explicit --author outranks detection, so following the published example replaces real harness and model provenance with a literal string and mislabels author_source as asserted. Second, tokens: the identity fragment is pure overhead repeated in every example an agent reads and in every command it then copies, which is the same budget the token-efficiency work is trying to shrink. The examples predate harness detection and were never revised when pm-z9x1r2 shipped. Every example should show the short form, and the one example that legitimately demonstrates an override should say why an override is the exception.

No published example passes --author or --assignee except the one example whose subject is identity override itself, and that example states why an override is the exception; A contract test asserts the identity-flag fragment appears in at most that one example across help content, operation registrations, docs, and scaffolds; Published examples are asserted to be the shortest form that still demonstrates the command's subject, with a measured token delta recorded as evidence on this item; The identity-override example is cross-referenced to the detection contract so the exception stays discoverable
The published example for every command is the shortest correct form of that command
Help text is the highest-leverage instruction surface pm has: an agent copies it far more often than it reads prose docs, so a wrong example is a defect multiplied by every agent that reads it
Shortens dozens of published examples, restores detected identity for agents that copy them, and removes repeated per-example token overhead
An agent that copies pm help verbatim produces minimal, correctly attributed commands
